summary_en: Interim dividend of 36 yen per share (3 yen increase) and year-end dividend forecast revised to 36 yen per share (3 yen increase), bringing full-year dividend to 72 yen, up 10 yen from prior year, following upward revision of full-year earnings forecast.
title_en: Notice Regarding Revision of Consolidated Business Forecast and Modification of Surplus Dividend (Interim Dividend) and Year-End Dividend Forecast (Dividend Increase)
translation_en_brief:
Shin-Etsu Polymer announced revisions to its dividend forecasts on October 26, 2026, following an upward revision of its consolidated earnings projection for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027. The company increased its interim dividend to 36 yen per share from the previously forecast 33 yen, representing a 3 yen increase. The year-end dividend forecast was similarly revised to 36 yen per share, also a 3 yen increase from the prior forecast of 33 yen. As a result, full-year dividend is now projected at 72 yen per share, an increase of 10 yen compared to the prior fiscal year's 62 yen per share.

The earnings revision reflected stronger-than-anticipated performance in semiconductor-related containers and wrapping films. The company raised its consolidated sales forecast for the fiscal year to 127 billion yen (from 120 billion yen), operating profit to 18.2 billion yen (from 16.0 billion yen), and net income attributable to parent company shareholders to 11.8 billion yen (from 10.5 billion yen).

The company stated that its dividend policy is based on maintaining financial soundness while securing resources for R&D investment, capital expenditures, and M&A activities, with the goal of providing stable, performance-linked dividends over the medium term. The interim dividend with an ex-dividend date of September 30, 2026, is scheduled to become effective on November 26, 2026.
